clue.text: Economy's bull! Period

parts.note: a steer is a young bull, castrated and raised for beef
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the expense of economists: their subject is all bull, full stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'Period!' reads as 'full stop' but is the wordplay's second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passenger accommodation on a ship, the old equivalent of economy class.

clue.text: Spoken about country life with no past

indicators.note: with no tells us to take the following word away from the word before it

parts.note: pastoral means concerning rural life and the countryside
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of an oral history of rural life that somehow leaves out the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral describes something delivered by voice rather than written, the same sense as spoken.

clue.text: Part with wartime scotch

indicators.note: Part says the answer is a part of the following words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of with into the start of wartime

explanation.surface: A tip-off that a bit of wartime whisky goes with something.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch here is the verb meaning to put an end to a plan or rumour, not the whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a scheme is to frustrate or put a stop to it, which is what thwarting does.

clue.text: Court held by peers drunk on spirit?

indicators.note: held by says the court abbreviation sits inside the letters that follow
drunk suggests the letters of peers reeling about out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal court presided over by members of the House of Lords who are intoxicated on spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit suggests drink to go with 'drunk', but it means a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or apparition, one sense of a spirit.

clue.text: Wannabee Egyptian killer gains terrorists' trust

indicators.note: gains says the following pieces are added on after the snake

parts.note: the asp is the Egyptian snake said to have killed Cleopatra
the IRA is the Irish Republican Army, the paramilitary group
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A would-be assassin from Egypt manages to win the confidence of a terrorist cell.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone hoping to achieve a position, informally called a wannabe.

clue.text: Mishit to putting surface for a birdie

parts.note: the green is the area of short grass around a golf hole where players putt
a shank is a golf shot struck off the heel of the club so it flies sideways

explanation.surface: A golfer's poor shot that nonetheless finds the green and sets up a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: Birdie is golf's one-under-par score in the surface, but here it simply means a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The greenshank is a wading bird of the sandpiper family, so it is a bird, affectionately a birdie.

clue.text: Lengthy north east rail fiasco?

indicators.note: a fiasco is a shambles, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble about a long-drawn-out shambles on the railway in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged along a line, extending in length only, hence lengthy in a loose sense.

clue.text: Celebrities' joint enterprise?

parts.note: celebrities are stars
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A business venture jointly owned by famous people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Enterprise is the famous starship of Star Trek; the question mark flags this capital-less example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enterprise is the spacecraft in Star Trek, so enterprise is an example of a starship.

clue.text: Paintings returned by popular demand

indicators.note: returned means the word for paintings is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: paintings are works of art, arts
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Pictures sent back to a gallery because the public asked for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a heavy demand placed on something, as in a strain on resources.

clue.text: Nick, Surrey opener, out for a duck

indicators.note: out says that letter is removed from the word before

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first

parts.note: the first letter of Surrey is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket report: Nick, the Surrey opening batsman, is dismissed without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county cricket team, and a duck is a batsman's score of zero; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck.

clue.text: One making theories of "Old Rockin'' Chair Got Me" by singer O'Connor

indicators.note: rocking sets the letters moving back and forth into a new order
got says the first word takes in the second, set side by side

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Des O'Connor was a British singer and television host

explanation.surface: It reads like a record listing: an old song title performed by Des O'Connor.
explanation.walkthrough: Des O'Connor was a popular British crooner and chat-show host; the old-song framing hides an ancient Greek thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mathematician from Syracuse devised theories of buoyancy and levers.

clue.text: Golf circuit strategy

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ambit is a boundary or circuit around something

explanation.surface: A tactic for getting round a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move or calculated ploy, a type of strategy.

clue.text: Nurse gives courage to charge of the 500?

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
a fee is a charge for a service
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A nurse gives bravery to the troops in a charge of five hundred, like the Light Brigade.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage; the surface evokes a famous cavalry charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a baby can mean feeding it, and bottle-feeding is one way of doing so.

clue.text: Confirm race ends with one, say, that can't lose

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of race are used
a means one

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the phrase is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: a cert is British slang for a certainty, a horse sure to win, so the thing that can't lose is a cert

explanation.surface: A tipster confirms that the race ends with a sure-fire winner in front.
explanation.walkthrough: A cert is British racing slang for a certainty; 'a cert' spoken aloud matches the second half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert something is to state it again firmly, to confirm it.

clue.text: Material for an SMS? I'll say!

parts.note: an SMS is a text message on a mobile phone

indicators.note: say tells us the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: I'll is pronounced like the ending of words such as tile

explanation.surface: Someone eager to send a mobile message on a topic shouts that they will.
explanation.definitionFit: Textile is woven fabric, or cloth, which is material.

clue.text: Not so much under the table as depressed

definitions.text: Not so much under the table
definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken cryptically: a drunk lists, so one less drunk lists less
second meaning: lacking energy and enthusiasm

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the answer into two words: someone 'under the table' is drunk and lists, or leans, so a less drunk person is 'list-less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lacking energy or interest, a common symptom of being low or depressed.

clue.text: Blasted Ed farts indiscriminately

indicators.note: indiscriminately means at random, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolboy joke about a man named Ed breaking wind all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with gunfire from low-flying aircraft, so strafed means blasted.

clue.text: Old queen into kinky work

parts.note: ex means former
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of the word are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former monarch who has got into some kinky activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Exertion is physical or mental effort, the sense of work as labour.

clue.text: Confiscate pen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to seize goods by legal authority
second meaning: an enclosure for stray animals

explanation.walkthrough: Pen suggests a writing tool but means an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for seizing property and a noun for the enclosure where stray animals or towed cars are held.

clue.text: Display of North America muscle is the government personified

indicators.note: a display is a show, here a rearranged showing of the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: American military might shown off as an embodiment of the state.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in stars-and-stripes is the national personification of the US federal government.

clue.text: Ecstasy in the sauna, perhaps, leads to ill-feeling?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given could be arranged another way

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking ecstasy in a sauna may make you feel unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Ill-feeling usually means resentment, but here it means physical sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is a sensation of sickness, literally a feeling of being ill.

clue.text: One in stud, perhaps, more cramped

indicators.note: in says the letter for one goes inside the card game

parts.note: stud is one variety of the card game poker

explanation.surface: A man at a stud farm, perhaps, finding things tighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Stud suggests a horse farm or an earring, but it is a form of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Poky describes a small, cramped room, so its comparative means more cramped.

clue.text: Powerful drug network

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
read as two words, net work: net is the fodder and work tells us to work its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of a strong narcotics distribution ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to split network into net and work: work, as in working dough, is the signal to rearrange the three letters of net.
explanation.definitionFit: Potent means having great power or strength, as of a drug or an argument.

clue.text: Working out daft clue of winter protection

indicators.note: working out a puzzle means rearranging its letters to solve it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver struggling with a silly clue about cold-weather gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffel coat is a heavy hooded woollen coat with toggles, worn against winter cold.

clue.text: Behind target

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an object of ridicule

explanation.walkthrough: Behind looks like a preposition but is the noun for one's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a person's bottom and also names someone who is the target of jokes.

clue.text: Make love with good French kiss initially

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the first letter of kiss is taken

explanation.surface: Romantic advice: start with a good French kiss before making love.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonk is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonk is informal British slang for having sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Break from depression

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pause or interval, as in school or parliament
second meaning: a hollow or alcove set into a wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Break from depression' reads as recovering from low mood; the two nouns are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a period of adjournment and an indentation or niche in a surface.

clue.text: Divorce for unorganised men?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken cryptically: the absence of a marriage union
second meaning: workers who do not belong to a trade union

explanation.walkthrough: Organised labour means unionised workers, so unorganised men are outside a union; a divorce leaves a marriage that is no longer a union.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes workers or firms not belonging to a trade union, and playfully a marriage dissolved.
